Package com.nexuslink.protocol.db

Class JdbcService

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.db.JdbcService
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class JdbcService extends Object implements AutoCloseable
Universal SQL client over JDBC. Holds a single connection for the session and runs statements synchronously (callers run it off the UI thread).

SQLite ships in-box; other databases work once their driver jar is on the classpath. The connection URL determines the database (e.g. jdbc:sqlite:/path/db, jdbc:postgresql://host/db, jdbc:mysql://host/db).

    • connect

      public void connect(String url, String user, String password, Map<String,String> extraProps) throws SQLException
      Opens a connection with extra driver properties (e.g. the TLS settings produced by JdbcTlsParams.forDriver(java.lang.String, com.nexuslink.protocol.db.JdbcTlsSpec)). Username/password are folded into the same property set, so the call works for embedded DBs (blank user) and TLS-only configs alike.
      Throws:
      SQLException

    • connectPooled

      public void connectPooled(JdbcConnectionPool pool, String url, String user, String password, Map<String,String> extraProps, JdbcPoolConfig config) throws SQLException
      Opens a pooled connection for this session through a caller-owned JdbcConnectionPool. The pool (a HikariDataSource keyed on URL + user) is created on first use and shared with any other service pointed at the same profile; this call borrows a single connection and holds it for the session, so the SQL editor/explorer behaviour is unchanged. close() returns the connection to the pool but leaves the pool itself running.
      Parameters:
      config - pool tuning (size/timeouts/validation); null uses JdbcPoolConfig.defaults()
      Throws:
      SQLException

    • setAutoCommit

      public void setAutoCommit(boolean autoCommit) throws SQLException
      Sets the session's auto-commit mode. When false, subsequent DML is buffered into an open transaction until commit() or rollback() — the model the SQL workbench uses to let a user edit several rows and then commit or discard them together.
      Throws:
      SQLException

    • isAutoCommit

      public boolean isAutoCommit()
      True if each statement commits immediately (the default). False while a manual transaction is open.

    • executeAll

      public int executeAll(List<String> statements) throws SQLException
      Runs several statements as a single unit and returns the total affected-row count. When the session is in auto-commit mode this wraps them in their own transaction (all-or-nothing, then auto-commit is restored); when a manual transaction is already open the statements simply join it, leaving the final commit/rollback to the caller. Used by the CSV importer.
      Throws:
      SQLException

    • execute

      public QueryResult execute(String sql, Map<String,String> values)
      Executes a statement that uses SQL Developer-style parameters, with values keyed by bare parameter name (see SqlBindVariables). :name binds go to the database as real JDBC parameters; &name substitutions are pasted into the SQL first.

      public void setServerOutputEnabled(boolean enabled) throws SQLException
      Turns the server-output panel on or off. On Oracle this also runs DBMS_OUTPUT.ENABLE/DISABLE, without which the server discards everything printed; elsewhere it just decides whether JDBC warnings are collected.
      Throws:

    • describeProcedure

      public CallableSpec describeProcedure(String routine) throws SQLException
      Reads a routine's parameter list from DatabaseMetaData, producing the CallableSpec the parameter form is built from. A procedureColumnReturn column makes it a function (rendered as {? = call …}); everything else becomes an IN, OUT or INOUT parameter carrying the database's own type name. Pass the bare routine name — the (function) suffix from listProcedures()/listFunctions() is stripped for you.
      Throws:
      SQLException

    • routineSource

      public String routineSource(String routine)
      Reads a routine's source text — the body the CREATE PROCEDURE / CREATE FUNCTION was written with, as far as the engine keeps it. The query is chosen from the connection URL by RoutineSource; Oracle's line-per-row form is joined back together.
      Returns:
      the source, or an empty string when the database does not expose it

    • routineSignature

      public String routineSignature(String routine)
      A readable one-line signature for a routine — name(IN a varchar, OUT b int) returns int — built from describeProcedure(java.lang.String), for the header above the source.

    • call

      public CallResult call(CallableSpec spec)
      Executes a stored procedure or function. IN values are bound as strings (drivers coerce, which is more portable than guessing a type here) with a blank/null value bound as SQL NULL; OUT and INOUT parameters are registered with the type from spec and read back afterwards. A routine that returns rows has them in CallResult.resultSet().

      public String erDiagramMermaid(Collection<String> onlyTables) throws SQLException
